week3_picks_results.stay_away: Noble vs Father Time: Noble won (143.38-94.62)

rankings.blurb: The throne sits comfortably. Mahomes’ 27.3 led the charge, McCaffrey rumbled for 23.1, and ARSB added 22.5 in a complete performance that pushed your winning streak to four games and your season points to 626.1. You’re 5-1 all-time against MHJTIME — a lopsided series that’s becoming a calling card — and the 13.12-point margin this week felt controlled, almost effortless. We spent the preseason questioning your RBs, your tight ends, your age profile. Through four weeks, the answers have been McCaffrey, Hunter Henry riding last week’s 25.0 energy, and “age is just a number if you have Mahomes.” Your Elo climbed another 15.8 points to 1604.3, and the Voltron receivers now have Voltron everything. The 2022 inaugural champion is the only undefeated team in the Jailyard, and the group chat owes you an apology. Collect it at 14-0.

Puka Nacua scored 29.5 points. In most weeks, that’s the kind of individual explosion that anchors a dominant win and earns you the high-scorer trophy. In Week 4, it earned you a 25.96-point loss to Ghastly Grayskull Gang, because the universe has a dark sense of humor. Baker Mayfield added 18.86, Garrett Wilson contributed 17.2, and Jonathan Taylor — coming off that 31.3 masterclass in Week 3 — came back to earth with 12.1. Your 150.46 would have beaten seven of the other eleven teams this week. You drew the one that scored 176.42. The defending champion’s first loss stung, and your Elo took the biggest hit of any team this week — a 31.9-point plunge. We called your consistency a personality trait. The consistency is still there; your opponent simply had a bigger scoreboard. Runner-up in 2022, runner-up in 2023, champion in 2024, and now 3-1 with a reminder that even dynasties have bad matchup weeks.

Maxx Crosby’s 23.0 and James Cook’s 21.0 powered a 149.18-point week that dispatched Chudders by 21.36, and more importantly, your 629.1 total season points are the most in the entire league. Let that register: the preseason twelfth-ranked team leads all twelve franchises in total scoring through four weeks. Lamar Jackson’s 11.68 was unusually quiet by Lamar standards, and Jake Ferguson’s 13.5 from the TE spot is the kind of sneaky production that doesn’t make the group chat but wins matchups. You’re 5-0 all-time against Chudders, a flawless record that says as much about your floor as their ceiling. The preseason said you were the instigator of side bets and polls. At 3-1 with the league’s highest point total, those side bets are starting to look prescient. The age cliff is still out there, but right now you’re running away from it.

One point six four. Josh Allen’s 25.86, Bucky Irving’s 23.0, and the Detroit Lions defense’s 20.0 added up to 155.66 — barely, just barely more than General Ken-obi’s 154.02 — and you have the upset of the week. The all-time series is now tied at three apiece, and the preseason essay that called you a “weekly thrill ride” just got its most thrilling evidence yet. Your Elo jumped 19.4 points to 1626.0, and Courtland Sutton’s 16.6 plus Achane’s 15.6 gave you enough depth to survive the closest finish of the season. Fifth in 2023. Fifth in 2024. And now 3-1 in 2025 with a win over the preseason favorite. The gravitational pull back to fifth is weakening. Whether it breaks entirely depends on what happens when the schedule stops gifting you decimals.

Josh Jacobs is thirty years old with over 1,500 career carries, and he just dropped 29.7 points like he was twenty-three and fresh out of Alabama. Jalen Hurts added 18.4, Dallas Goedert contributed 17.7, and the Houston Texans defense pitched in 16.0 in a 166.0-point performance that demolished Burden by 31.6. You’re on a two-game winning streak, sitting at 3-1, and outperforming both preseason top-three teams above you. The preseason essay said the name says it all: aging stars that could awaken for one more run. Four weeks in, the alarm clock is blaring. Your head-to-head advantage over Burden is now 4-2, and the league’s softest schedule is proving more expressway than uphill climb. You rode Hurts and a deep backfield to the 2024 final, and the formula hasn’t changed. The window isn’t closing. It just got new hinges.

Three down. The preseason number one took its first loss, and it came by the cruelest margin imaginable: 1.64 points against a team everyone had ranked below you. Drake Maye’s 23.22 and Drake London’s 22.0 were excellent. Kevin Byard’s 18.0 from the IDP slot was a bonus. Saquon Barkley and Kenneth Walker combined for 26.9 from the RB room that was supposed to be the league’s best. It wasn’t enough. Your Elo remains the highest in the league at 1700.2 — a number that screams “still the team to beat” even as the record now reads “mortal.” The franchise everyone measures themselves against just got measured by Rasheeing the Scene, and the all-time series is knotted at three. We said in the preseason that your depth would win you boring games. This week was the opposite: a game where depth lost to decimals. The taxi squad debates can wait. The question now is whether one loss is a blip or a fault line.

Remember when the preseason said your pick stash was bigger than your WR room? DK Metcalf dropped 21.1, Quentin Johnston added 19.8, and Xavier Worthy contributed 14.6 — three receivers combining for 55.5 points in a week where the “thin receiver room” narrative went up in smoke. Omarion Hampton’s 25.0 led the scoring, C.J. Stroud orchestrated with 18.42, and your 176.42 total was the highest in the league. You beat the defending champion by 25.96. Your Elo spiked 31.9 points — the biggest jump of any team this week. Two straight wins, two straight weeks climbing the rankings, and the chat’s “picks don’t score points” refrain is officially retired. The consolation-bracket-to-contender story just got its breakout chapter, and Hampton hitting is exactly the preseason condition we flagged for contention. Whether this is a two-week hot streak or a season-defining emergence is the question that will define your next month.

Bijan Robinson’s 25.1 led the way, and a surprise Javonte Williams 17.5 performance gave the backfield a new wrinkle nobody saw coming. Tyler Warren added 15.8, Breece Hall kicked in 13.6, and the Chicago Bears defense contributed 13.0 in a 48.76-point demolition of Father Time that was the biggest blowout of the week. You’re 2-2 with back-to-back wins after that 0-2 start, and the “scariest backfield in the league” is beginning to look the part again. The preseason listed you at number two; the current rankings have you eighth. That gap tells the story of a roster better on paper than on the field — but two consecutive wins suggest the paper version is catching up to reality. Father Time’s 94.62 made this one feel like batting practice, and the real test comes next week against Ken-obi. Tyler Warren might be the TE answer you didn’t know you had.

The freefall continued. Your top scorer was Quinshon Judkins at 19.5 — a running back, on a roster where three historic wide receivers are supposed to carry the scoring load. Marvin Harrison Jr. managed 15.6. The New England Patriots defense scored 16.0. Geno Smith posted 12.78 at quarterback. Chase, Nabers, and Harrison Jr. have been invisible for two consecutive weeks, and the 133.68-point total wasn’t enough against a Legion squad that’s now 5-1 all-time against you. The preseason called you a contender. The preseason said “toilet bowl runner-up in 2023, semifinalist in 2024, top three in 2025.” Through four weeks, it’s looking more like regression to the mean. Your Elo dropped another 15.8 to 1585.7, and that “what if” label from the preseason essay isn’t a warning anymore — it’s a biography. At 1-3, you’re running out of weeks to prove the models wrong and running into the reality that even the best WR trio in dynasty can’t overcome a roster that’s misfiring everywhere else.

George Pickens exploded for 29.4 points, Justin Jefferson added 17.6, and Kyler Murray contributed 18.1 — actual offensive production from your star players for once. And you still lost by 31.6. The Sleeping Giants ran you over behind Josh Jacobs’ 29.7, and the head-to-head series moves to 4-2 in their favor. Your 134.4 total was your best output of the season, which is both encouraging and deeply depressing — encouraging because it proves the talent can score, depressing because even your best week produces a blowout loss. The preseason called you a cautionary tale of stars without support. Four weeks in, the cautionary tale has become a full novel. Jefferson still hasn’t led the league in scoring in any single week. The trade whispers are now trade plans. At 0-4 with a 1323.5 Elo near the league floor, “fraud tier” has stopped being a prediction and started being a diagnosis.

Ninety-four point six two. That’s the number. The lowest score of the week by a country mile, and the kind of output that makes the group chat wince rather than roast. Aidan Hutchinson’s 19.5 from the defensive line was your top scorer — an IDP player leading your scoring column is the fantasy equivalent of your left tackle being your best offensive weapon. Rome Odunze added 14.9, Jared Goff posted 13.72, and Davante Adams kicked in 13.6 in a week where nothing clicked and everything hurt. Noble FFT beat you by 48.76 — the biggest blowout of the season — and your Elo cratered 23.5 points to 1329.9. The preseason said the chat would love your random 180-point weeks. Four weeks in, your season high is 165.06 from Week 2. The wagyu beef WRs are spoiling, the ramen noodle RBs are still ramen noodles, and the kitchen is officially closed. The spoiler role requires actually winning games.

Ashton Jeanty scored 32.5 points. The top individual performer in the entire league this week plays for you. And you lost by 21.36. That’s the rebuild in one sentence: the future is absurdly talented, and the present is absurdly painful. Emeka Egbuka added 18.1, Gibbs contributed 16.7, and Herbert posted 15.52 — an RB-heavy scoring profile that’s actually exactly what the long-term blueprint calls for. The Boonist Monks are 5-0 all-time against you, and that perfect record is less about talent gaps and more about roster completeness — you have explosive parts without a functioning whole. The preseason said you were playing for 2026, and nothing about 0-4 changes that timeline. But Jeanty’s 32.5 is a preview of what those picks and prospects are building toward. You’re bench-pressing next to the trophy case, and the weights just got lighter. The war chest remains. The patience is required. But the glimpses are getting louder.

confessionals.text: One point six four. I checked the score three times. Then I checked it again. Josh Allen delivered, Bucky Irving delivered, and we won by a margin thinner than the charge on my phone at kickoff. The group chat went silent for exactly twelve seconds when the final scores posted. I counted. Twelve seconds. That’s the longest silence this league has ever produced. We just beat the preseason number one. We just tied the all-time series. I’m framing the box score.

They told me my WR room was thin. They told me my pick stash was bigger than my receiver corps. Then DK Metcalf went off for 21.1, Quentin Johnston scored 19.8, and I hung 176 on the defending champion. The Lock of the Week was Kittler beating me. The Lock. Of the Week. I’d like to thank this column for the motivation. Bulletin board material hits different when you’re holding the highest score of the week.

I have three of the best wide receivers in dynasty football. Ja’Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, Marvin Harrison Jr. I also have Geno Smith playing quarterback and a defense outscoring my WR2. The preseason said I was a contender. The standings say I’m 1-3. The group chat says nothing because even they feel bad. When the roasters go quiet, you know it’s real.

Ashton Jeanty scored 32.5 points. Thirty-two and a half. The top performer in the entire league. On my team. We lost by 21. I’m not even mad at this point — I’m impressed by the universe’s commitment to the bit. Jeanty and Gibbs are going to be terrifying in 2026. In 2025, they’re terrifying on a team that’s 0-4. The war chest remains.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: The Lock of the Week was Kittler minus five over Ghastly. Ghastly won by 25.96. Should we rename it the Rock of the Weak?
mailbag.answer: The Lock of the Week is currently under internal investigation. What we can confirm: Puka Nacua scored 29.5 and it didn’t matter. What we cannot confirm: whether this column has any business gambling with your emotions. The Lock will return next week with its reputation in tatters and its confidence somehow intact.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: Ken-obi lost by 1.64 points. Is that the thinnest margin of the season?
mailbag.answer: It is. And it might be the most significant margin too. The preseason number one taking its first loss on the thinnest edge of the season, to a team stuck in fifth for two years, with the all-time series now tied at three? That’s not just a close game. That’s a narrative shift wrapped in a decimal point.

mailbag.question: @Chudders asks: My best player scored 32.5 and I still lost. At what point do I just start celebrating individual performances?
mailbag.answer: You start now. The rebuild isn’t measured in wins this year — it’s measured in Jeanty scoring like a top-three fantasy asset and Gibbs adding 16.7 in the same game. Think of each loss as a down payment on a penthouse you can’t move into yet.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: MHJTIME’s WR trio has disappeared for two straight weeks. Is it time to panic?
mailbag.answer: It was time to panic last week. Now it’s time to diagnose. Chase, Nabers, and Harrison Jr. haven’t been the top three scorers on their own roster in any week this season. The talent is undeniable. The context around it — Geno Smith at quarterback, a defense outscoring your WR2 — is a crime scene.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: The Legion of Bouz is 4-0. Did we all just not see this coming?
mailbag.answer: We literally ranked them ninth. Ninth! The inaugural champion had the preseason resume of a frisky spoiler, and four weeks later they’re the only undefeated team with Mahomes, McCaffrey, and ARSB forming a big three that looks like the 2008 Celtics — older, wiser, and apparently unbothered by the age curves the rest of us keep citing.

bits.title: Preseason Prediction Tracker
bits.text: Week 3 picks went 3-3, bringing the cumulative record to 11-7. The Lock of the Week (Kittler -5.0 over Ghastly) cratered — the biggest Lock bust of the season, with Ghastly winning by 25.96. The Upset Watch (MHJTIME +4.0 over Legion) also missed. The Stay Away (Noble vs Father Time) stayed away from competitive — Noble won by 48.76. This column’s gambling advice: profitable overall, devastating in specifics.

bits.title: Luck Index
bits.text: Rasheeing the Scene winning by 1.64 over General Ken-obi is the season’s luckiest result. Re-simulate that matchup a thousand times and Ken-obi wins most of them. Meanwhile, Father Time’s 94.62 against Noble’s 143.38 wasn’t luck — that was inevitability wearing a scoreboard.

bits.title: Overheard in the Chat
bits.text: ‘I lost to a team that was the Lock to lose’ — @bchodos, who scored 150.46 and somehow lost by 25.96. ‘Jeanty scored 32.5 and we still lost. I’ve decided losses are just his origin story’ — @Chudders, finding beauty in the rubble.

bits.title: Things I Believe But Can’t Prove
bits.text: The Legion of Bouz won’t lose until Week 7. MHJTIME’s WR trio will all score 20+ in the same week before Week 8. Father Time will score 170 in a loss because the universe requires it. And Ashton Jeanty will finish as the overall RB1 on a team that finishes 2-12.

bits.title: Is Ghastly the New Sleeping Giants?
bits.text: The preseason had them ranked low, the chat doubted their roster, and then the breakout happened. Ghastly’s 176.42 echoes the Sleeping Giants’ 2024 run from the bottom half to the championship game. The difference: Ghastly’s core isn’t aging. Omarion Hampton and C.J. Stroud are both in their early twenties. If this is the breakout, the ceiling is higher than the Giants ever had.

picks.blurb: Two 3-1 squads, but the Monks have the most total points in the league at 629.1 and Lamar Jackson has a 149-point floor this week. Kittler is licking wounds after a 25.96-point loss and the Elo took a 31.9-point hit — the biggest drop in the league. Puka Nacua can explode any given week, but Cook, Crosby, and Lamar at home is the safer side.

Two sinking ships, but one has life rafts. MHJTIME’s roster — Chase, Nabers, Harrison Jr. — is too talented to stay down forever, and Burden’s 0-4 start with a 487.1 total PF is the league’s weakest output. If the historic WR trio wakes up even partially, this one’s over early.

Ken-obi’s 1.64-point loss was a fluke, not a collapse. Drake Maye, Saquon Barkley, and CeeDee Lamb still comprise the deepest roster in the league, and Noble’s 2-2 start from the preseason two-spot suggests they’re still finding their footing. Ken-obi bounces back in what should be a statement game.

The 4-0 juggernaut hosts a 3-1 Giants squad riding Josh Jacobs’ 29.7-point eruption. On paper this is competitive — both teams are rolling. But the Legion has Mahomes, McCaffrey, and ARSB firing on all cylinders and the longest active winning streak in the league. Trust the unbeaten until someone proves otherwise.

Father Time’s 94.62 was a season low, and Josh Allen isn’t the type to let a team riding a 1.64-point upset high come back down to earth. Rasheeing is 3-1 with the league’s best quarterback and an RB room that showed up in force last week. This one could get ugly fast.

Ghastly just hung 176.42 on the defending champion and Hampton is running hot. Chudders has Jeanty — who dropped 32.5 last week — and a war chest of young talent that could explode on any given Sunday. The talent gap favors Ghastly, but Chudders’ boom-or-bust potential makes this one spicier than the spread suggests.
